attempts.summary: Configured sudo on node1 to log every sudo invocation (user, timestamp, PWD, command) to a dedicated /var/log/sudo-commands.log via an /etc/sudoers.d/99-command-logging drop-in (Defaults logfile=..., log_input/log_output, !syslog), which also suppresses sudo's normal syslog/authpriv output so entries no longer land in the general system log (/var/log/secure). Verified before and after a full node reboot: dedicated log captured new sudo commands, secure log's sudo-line count stayed flat (14→14 pre-restart, 44→44 post-restart), and the node's boot id changed (4cee4ea8... → 772e50f6...) confirming an actual restart with the config surviving it.
